newsitem.title: MEXICO: Four groups vie for Mexico's northeast rail line.
newsitem.headline: Four groups vie for Mexico's northeast rail line.

text.p: Four investor groups have expressed interest in bidding for 80 percent of Ferrocarril del Noreste, the second rail line to be put up for auction after the first sale was voided due to low bidding.
Aaron Dychter, undersecretary of Communications and Transport, said three of those groups were already authorized to bid while another has shown interest.
He said the three authorized groups are:
-- One formed by GEC Alsthom, France's Societe Nationale des Chemins de Fer and Mexico's Grupo Olmeca, which has insurance and cable interests
-- A group led by Mexican builder ICA and Southwestern Bell Corp
-- A third made up of Transportacion Maritima Mexicana and Kansas City Southern Industries.
The fourth group involves Grupo Mexico, the mining firm whose bid for the Chihuahua-Pacific line this week was rejected by the government as being too low.
Dychter said Grupo Mexico could link up with Illinois Central, South Orient and a group of former officials of Southern Pacific.
Bidding for the line, considered a key one on offer, is slated for November 29. He said it was still not decided whether the Chihuahua-Pacific line would be included in the northeast package.
